business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Pet Supplies and Pet Care Devices

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-code tradition, unitary national regulation, heavy EU-law harmonization; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–People's Republic of China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 17 March 1994; amended by Protocol signed 22 March 2019; in force)
Agreement between the Benelux Economic Union and the People's Republic of China on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 3 June 1984; in force since 1 January 1986)

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (signed 3 April 1996; as amended; in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (consolidated, last amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 20/744; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on identification of beneficial owners; Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq. on money laundering.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access to the Luxembourg RBE is suspended following the ECJ judgments of 22 November 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; access is granted to Luxembourg competent authorities, the financial intelligence unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier), and AML/CFT obliged entities acting within statutory due diligence)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder, manager and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or notary of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention of 5 October 1961) or Consular Legalization for non-Hague issuers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-bankruptcy or extract of criminal record (bulletin no. 3 or foreign equivalent) for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal record registry of the manager's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good-standing extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement not older than three months) of each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or licensed credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or preliminary account-opening approval for the corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution in the beneficiary's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association (statuts) in French or German reflecting the reserved company name
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not applicable - executed before the Luxembourg notary at incorporation; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, managers and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List and the OFAC 50-Percent Rule, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Luxembourg national sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, and national and international PEP registers. Screening is repeated at account opening and continuously during the relationship; all results are documented in the AML/CFT client file under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 20/744. A positive sanctions hit triggers immediate funds blocking and reporting to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier; a positive PEP hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS ePortal (www.lbr.lu) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; name reservation is applied for by the drafting notary through the RCS electronic filing platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the standard statutory drafting language; company names may be formed in Luxembourgish, French or German using Latin-script characters, and a non-Latin foreign name must be transliterated into Latin characters with a French or German transliteration disclosed. The legal-form suffix SARL or Société à responsabilité limitée is mandatory; the name must be visually and phonetically distinguishable from existing RCS entries, must not mislead as to the corporate object or legal form, and must not infringe public order or third-party rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Bankers (requires Ministry of Finance prior authorization)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires CSSF prior authorization)
Fonds d'investissement / SICAV / SIF / Investment Fund (regulated reserve)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Marché financier (requires Ministry of Finance prior authorization)
État / Gouvernement / National / Communal (state or public-authority connotation prohibited)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross and international-organization denominations (reserved)
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce (reserved statutory chamber)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the notary or the applicant may file a reasoned re-examination request with the RCS Registration Office within 15 days of the refusal notice, with the amended denomination and the applicable re-filing fee; a refusal grounded on public order or deceptive denomination may be appealed before the competent chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within a further 15 days of notification. The name reservation may be renewed for one additional 30-day term before expiry; in all cases the notarial incorporation deed must be executed before the reservation lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this industry. A pure virtual arrangement is permitted only through a commercial domiciliation agent licensed by the Ministry of the Economy under the Law of 31 May 1999, which supplies a physical registered-office address in Luxembourg, service-of-process capacity and mail handling. Since ISIC 4791 electronic retailing of pet supplies requires no statutory license and is rated low AML risk, domiciliation without leased premises is structurally accepted, provided the company maintains local books, board decisions and e-commerce operational records to evidence economic substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low in the standard scenario: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by the RCS registration officers, Economic Ministry delegates or tax authorities for a low-risk, license-exempt e-commerce SARL with a compliant UBO and registered-office file. The probability rises to 25-35% upon sustained UBO register discrepancies, adverse media or sanctions hits, or financial-risk flags reported by payment providers (Stripe, PayPal) or the financial intelligence unit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing and publication fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-document tariff (approximately USD 60-90 per apostille) plus handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff plus courier market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 et seq. (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on Accounting and Annual Accounts
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation comprising the articles of association) filed for RCS registration and RESA publication
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital EUR 12,000; at least EUR 6,000 (50%) must be fully paid up at formation; cash contributions must be deposited on a bank account blocked in the name of the company until RCS registration; the remaining 50% must be paid within five years
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation deed and articles of association be executed by the appointed notary; The subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000 is approved and the statutory minimum of EUR 6,000 is confirmed credited to the blocked corporate account; The registered office of the Company is adopted at the address indicated in the articles of association; [NAME] is appointed sole manager (gérant) with full powers of administration, banking authority, and representation; The manager is authorized to complete the RCS filing, RESA publication, establishment authorization, VAT registration, and ancillary formalities; No industrial establishment license is required, the object being exclusively the online retail of pet products and supplies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the LBR e-portal or the notary's query channel to confirm the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry; no formal reservation is mandatory, but a preliminary availability certificate is recommended before notarial drafting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusingly similar, amend the name suffix and re-submit in writing; negative-presumption objections are cured by adopting a distinctive second element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of articles of association and statutory capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public acting on behalf of the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators convene before a Luxembourg notary to sign the notarial deed of incorporation; simultaneously the cash share capital is transferred to a bank account opened in the name of the company in formation, blocked for the benefit of the future company; the notary verifies the capital deposit certificate and the substance of the articles prepared under the Law of 10 August 1915.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or ID cards of incorporators
Bank capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage)
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the draft (e.g., capital deposit mismatch or missing power of attorney), cure by rectifying the deed, supplementing the dossier, or using the Guichet.lu single point of formalities; the notary may ask for a new deposit certificate only when the previous is stale.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of first board resolution and officer appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General meeting of shareholders / appointed manager (internal act, no registry filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribers approve the initial capital subscription, adopt the registered office, and appoint the manager (gérant); the resolution is recorded in the minutes of the constitutive general meeting and countersigned by the subscribers to evidence the appointment for the RCS filing; maintain the minute in the corporate register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the civil-law judge or notary finds a governance defect, adopt a rectifying shareholders' resolution within the same deed or by supplementary notarial act before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and RESA statutory publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically files the incorporation deed with the RCS through the e-RCS service; the RCS performs legal and formal scrutiny, attributes a RCS registration number, and publishes the instrument in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) within the set deadline; legal personality commences on the date of RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Formalized filing form signed by the manager
Proof of manager's identity and legal capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an omission or a defect notice, cure within the imposed delay by filing corrective particulars online; any late publication is regularized through a rectifying filing and, if required, a notarial addendum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME et de l'Entrepreneuriat (e-process via guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The manager submits the establishment authorization application for the commercial retail e-commerce activity via Guichet.lu with proof of personal professional integrity and, where the activity is not regulated, the statutory declaration; the authorization must be obtained before commencing e-commerce trading; the e-commerce sale of pet supplies is an unregulated commercial activity, but the trading authorization is still mandatory under the Law of 2 September 2011.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of manager
Proof of professional qualification or declaration of unregulated status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, the administration issues a solicitation; supplement the dossier electronically within the granted deadline; refusals are appealable before the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, corporate income tax and registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration and the flat-rate municipal business tax declaration via the MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-space; obtain the Luxembourg VAT number for cross-border e-commerce; register for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and registration tax; submit the annual accounts filing profile to the RCS/LBR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or contested registration letters are cured by filing the missing fiscal form and paying any late-payment interest; objections to a VAT determination are appealable in writing to AEDT within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security registration of the manager and potential employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the manager, if subject to Luxembourg social security, and any future e-commerce staff with CCSS before hiring; implement the mandatory declaration of wages and electronic payslips; this step is mandatory as soon as the SARL remunerates natural persons.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is late or queried, file retroactive declarations with supporting contracts and pay any assessments; disputes are handled through the CCSS administrative procedure and the Social Security Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-commerce operational registrations (data protection and consumer compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD); Ministry of the Economy - consumer affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a data protection officer if processing at scale, conclude GDPR compliance documentation and maintain the processing register; implement the distance-selling information duties (price, delivery, 14-day withdrawal right) on the pet supplies e-commerce platform; no separate e-commerce permit exists for EU cross-border online selling.
required_dossiers: Terms and conditions of the online shop
Withdrawal and returns policy (14-day EU Consumer Rights Directive)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CNPD queries are rectified through responsive documentation and record updates; consumer complaints may be settled by modifying the legal notice and contracts; in case of non-cooperation, the CNPD can issue warnings or fines - cure by implementing its corrective orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial establishment; commercial e-commerce activity is governed by the Law of 2 September 2011 through the Ministry of the Economy (establishment authorization already covered in SOP Step 5)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no manufacturing permit required; the operating authorization for the SARL is the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency, under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Classified installations (commodo) only apply to operations exceeding de minimis thresholds; pure electronic retailing and office/warehouse storage of finished pet products fall outside the mandatory EIA list; if a small warehouse is added, check the commune's commodo permit (Class 4/5) and confirm the declaration-free status
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions expected; waste handling compliant with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, packaging waste reporting obligations under extended producer responsibility (EPR) for product packaging, and municipal collection rules; if logistical storage is operated, comply with occupational hygiene thresholds and fire-safety codes only, not with IPPC/IED emission thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: if the SARL operates an office or storage space exceeding the commune capacity thresholds, the building must be cleared by the Service national de la protection civile (CGDIS) and the local fire prevention office, with evacuation plans and extinguishers; occupational: registration with the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) as employer, compliance with the Labor Code on workplace ergonomics, electrical installations and first-aid, plus a medical check by a certified occupational physician; structural load inspection only required for racked storage over statutory limits

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; VAT administered by Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Corporate and fiscal registration is effected through Le Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the official e-portal MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-resident SARL obtains a single national identification number (matricule) from the RCS upon incorporation through a Luxembourg-registered notary; the matricule functions as the corporate tax file number for ACD. Before commencing taxable e-commerce activity, the SARL must register for VAT with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu and receive a Luxembourg VAT identification number. A foreign non-resident e-commerce operator must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative for Luxembourg VAT unless it uses the Union/Non-Union One-Stop Shop regime; there is no registration threshold for non-EU sellers. EU sellers of pet supplies into Luxembourg are subject to the EUR 10,000 annual distance-sale threshold for Luxembourg VAT registration or OSS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Luxembourg-resident S.à r.l. is an opaque capital company subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; no default pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective hybrid look-through regime exists under Luxembourg law. Taxable person may elect: (1) fiscal integration tax consolidation with Luxembourg/EEA subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at 95% for a five-year commitment; (2) VAT grouping as a Single Taxable Person for VAT; (3) small-undertaking VAT exemption by resident small enterprises only. Anti-hybrid provisions follow ATAD; no elective hybrid mismatch treatment is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-enterprise exemption: annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 30,000 (optional and inapplicable to non-resident sellers). Cross-border intra-EU distance sales into Luxembourg: EUR 10,000 per calendar year threshold, above which Luxembourg VAT registration or OSS is mandatory. Non-EU sellers: registration with AEDT is required as from the first euro of Luxembourg taxable B2C supplies, subject to marketplace deemed-supplier rules for electronically facilitated e-commerce.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no mandatory real-time B2B e-invoicing clearance regime, no continuous transaction controls, and no fiscal digital stamping. Electronic invoicing is accepted for VAT compliance; B2G invoices must be transmitted electronically through the national e-procurement government platform. Luxembourg is preparing EU ViDA transposition with expected structured e-invoicing obligations after 2030; cross-border customs e-procedures are cleared electronically under the Union Customs Code via the AES/ECS systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Pet supplies and pet-care devices sold by the SARL to non-EU customers qualify for 0% Luxembourg VAT as export supplies if the goods physically leave the EU within the statutory dispatch period and the supplier retains comprehensive export evidence, including a customs export declaration naming the SARL as exporter, transport documentation showing exit from the EU, and proof of payment from the non-EU buyer. Offshore services to non-EU business customers are zero-rated where place-of-supply rules place the supply outside Luxembourg; B2C digital services are instead taxable in the customer's jurisdiction and fall under the non-Union OSS, not Luxembourg VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (e-Export AES/ECS declaration with Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, alternatively CMR road consignment note evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or payment receipt evidencing full remittance of export sale proceeds from the non-EU buyer
Proof of exit (customs electronic exit confirmation or transport/handler evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating is claimed without complete or genuine export proof, the AEDT/ACD may retrospectively disallow the 0% rate, assess Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the supply, and charge late-payment interest. Administrative fines may reach up to 100% of the evaded tax under the Luxembourg General Tax Law. Deliberate fraudulent export VAT juggling is a criminal tax offense punishable by fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to five years; cross-border cases also trigger Eurofisc and mutual assistance exchanges under Council Regulation (EU) No 904/2010.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), exercising prudential and statistical functions jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which supervises credit institutions and enforces the Luxembourg AML/CFT law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF regulatory circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full liberalisation. Luxembourg maintains no foreign-exchange controls; both capital and current account transactions benefit from unrestricted convertibility under TFEU Articles 63–66, the Luxembourg law of 27 December 2003 on free movement of capital, and ECB free-transfer regulations. Profit and dividend remittances require no exchange-control authorisation; the only constraint is fiscal, being the standard 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, reducible to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders holding a direct participation of at least 10% for at least 12 months under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Article 147 LIR domestic exemption.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no minimum EUR conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export receipts. Export receivables may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency, but must be recorded in EUR equivalent under the Luxembourg Commercial Code accounting framework and supported by compliant commercial invoices for CIT and VAT purposes; intra-group cross-border flows must be documented at arm's length under Luxembourg transfer-pricing rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for the pre-selected rails: Stripe operates under EEA e-money passporting via Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Ireland), while PayPal operates through PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie S.C.A., itself domiciled in Luxembourg and authorised by the CSSF as a credit institution – both are structurally compatible with the Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 4791 e-commerce model. A Luxembourg-licensed fallback EMI, Mangopay S.A., is available for marketplace or sub-merchant fund flows. Offshore third-country digital EMIs without a PSD2 passport or CSSF equivalence authorisation may not lawfully service Luxembourg merchants and are rated Not Viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 banks generally require physical presence of at least one appointed managing director (gérant) during initial onboarding, or a notarially executed and apostilled power of attorney held by a Luxembourg-resident mandated agent. BCEE and BGL BNP Paribas permit hybrid video-first identity verification for low-risk e-commerce SARLs, but final account activation requires an in-person visit by a signatory or an equivalent certified onboarding through a CRA-verified digital mandate, accompanied by the current RBE extract (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) and certified company constitutional documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: UBO(s) holding more than 25% are not conclusively identified, or the RBE filing is inconsistent with the bank signatory mandate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date RBE extract certificate; share register; notarial articles of incorporation and deed of appointment of the gérant; passport copies of all UBOs; signed AML declarations confirming natural-person UBOs and absence of nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concern on initial capital: the minimum SARL capital of €12,000 is funded by a third-country shareholder without documentary wealth trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Origin-of-funds declaration (déclaration d'origine des fonds); 12-month bank statements of the funding account; underlying sale, inheritance, or employment contracts explaining wealth accumulation; notarial attestation of blocked capital deposit; and prior-period financial statements if the shareholder is a corporate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce red flags: elevated chargeback/refund ratios, card-not-present transaction spikes, or recurring payment traffic from high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements; published refund and chargeback policy; customer complaint logs; transaction-level reporting and reconciliation records; logistics contracts with bills of lading; and supplier sourcing invoices evidencing genuine physical pet-supply trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency: non-resident management with no verifiable Luxembourg office, payroll, or board decision-making footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg registered-office lease agreement; employment contracts or payroll evidence; board meeting minutes held in Luxembourg; business plan and marketing budget for the EU-facing e-commerce operation; website infrastructure and domain records; and supplier/customer contracts negotiated from Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder capital contribution must be wired via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-resident shareholders) to the SARL's blocked capital escrow account opened at BCEE or BGL prior to notarial incorporation, stating the CSSF/ECB balance-of-payments statistical purpose code for equity capital subscription. The beneficiary account name must exactly match the provisional SARL corporate name, the remitter must be the named shareholder, and the notary receives a bank blockage attestation; funds are released to the operational account only after the notarial deed is signed and the RBE filing is completed. Any third-country-sourced transfer must be accompanied by a source-of-funds declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Non-Eurozone supplier settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 through correspondent banking rails, including Luxembourg RMB clearing lines operated by Chinese bank branches for pet-product sourcing from Asia; EU supplier payments and consumer refunds are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant; high-value containerised imports are supported by documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) issued by BGL or BIL with confirmation added by the beneficiary's bank; and Stripe/PayPal card settlement flows are swept in EUR to the Luxembourg operational account through the providers' standard payout rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD FX swaps and rollover forwards
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for RMB-denominated import exposure
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for supplier credit lines or LC refinancing
Bought vanilla FX options (calls and puts) subject to MiFID II appropriateness and EMIR reporting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and management report, approved by shareholders and filed with the Luxembourg trade and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved by the general meeting within 6 months of the financial year-end; filing with the RCS and publication in RESA must occur within 1 month after approval (maximum 7 months after year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposed to judicial fine up to EUR 5,000 (court discretion), forced filing at director's expense, and possible administrative dissolution/strike-off upon persistent default; sanctions recorded on company's RCS extract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) - Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter (by 31 March at latest) for companies with a calendar year; foreign fiscal year entities confirm within one month following the anniversary date of the initial declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal and administrative fines up to EUR 1,250 per infraction; repeated non-confirmation can trigger formal warnings and potential strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur les revenus collectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the following calendar year; electronically filed returns may obtain an automatic extension to 30 September.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment by tax office, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax (cap 10%), and fines for failure to file up to EUR 10,000 or imprisonment in persistent cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Bureau d'imposition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same calendar schedule as CIT return: generally by 31 May; extension via e-filing to 30 September.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and interest (0.6% per month) on the assessed net wealth tax; possible enforcement proceedings and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit for SARL when, at financial year-end, the undertaking exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50 employees. Audit is also obligatory if the SARL is a public interest entity, parent of a group exceeding these thresholds, or when the articles stipulate an audit for minority shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) as prescribed by the Law of 19 December 2002; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for statutory accounts when legally required or optionally under conditions. Consolidated accounts must use IFRS if the group exceeds the mandatory consolidation thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SARL must verify and confirm that the beneficial owner information recorded in the RBE is accurate, complete and current. Share transfers causing a change in shareholding of 25% or more (or in voting rights) must be reported to the RBE within one month of the transfer. As part of the annual confirmation, the company must re-affirm the identity details and attest the continuing accuracy of the UBO data; no duplicate register is needed but the internal register of UBOs must be updated and kept on-site.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholder meetings and board/manager decisions)
Register of UBOs (beneficial owners) with historical audit trail

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 (annual registered office/agent services including compliance mailbox, signposting, and RCS/RBE coordination)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 18,000 (typical for an e-commerce SARL without complex consolidation, subject to corporate structure and turnover)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate in Luxembourg City for fiscal 2024/2025, comprising corporate income tax at 17%, unemployment fund contribution at 0.3%, and municipal business tax at 7.5%; municipal business tax varies by commune between 6.75% and 11.025%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box grants an 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income and gains, yielding an effective CIT rate of approximately 5.27%. Notional Interest Deduction on qualifying new equity reduces taxable base. Investment tax credits for digital and ecological assets and the participation exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains can further lower the effective rate. No general preferential rate applies to pure e-commerce trading income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically through the eCAB portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); corporate income tax return for the SARL.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. One Form 510 is filed per fiscal year; quarterly advance CIT payments are made based on the most recent assessment, and a nil-high transaction SDDS is not required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a SARL with a 31 December year-end, the return is due by 31 December of the following year, unless a written extension is granted by the ACD; the administration may also demand an earlier filing date by formal reminder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before tax per the statutory annual accounts, including e-commerce sales through Stripe/PayPal, cost of goods sold, fulfilment costs, payment-processing fees, marketing, software costs and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident SARL must declare its worldwide income. Foreign shareholders do not report items on this form. All revenue must be reconciled with payment-processor settlement reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (income tax, municipal business tax, excessive director fees, penalties, undocumented cash payments) and subtraction of deductible items (IP box exemption, notional interest deduction, investment tax credits, prior-year losses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A detailed tax-adjustment schedule and transfer-pricing documentation should be attached if related-party transactions exceed statutory thresholds. Non-resident intercompany charges must be arm's length and economically substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 510 attachments — Renseignements concernant les associés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of shareholders, their country of residence, shareholding percentages, dividend distribution history and beneficial ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the tax identification number, country of residence and direct/indirect ownership chain for each non-resident shareholder. The ACD uses this information to assess withholding tax relief and substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions, including online marketplace positioning, payment processor agreements, procurement of pet-product inventories, app development services and management fees paid to foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the value of controlled transactions exceeds EUR 500,000, a Local File reflecting OECD transfer-pricing principles must be available upon ACD request. Foreign ultimate parent group consolidating above EUR 750 million must ensure a Master File is in place.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment expose the SARL to default interest at 0.6% per month on outstanding CIT, a penalty up to EUR 5,000 for non-submission, and possible 'taxation d'office' where the ACD assesses the tax on a lump-sum basis. Deliberate concealment escalates to criminal tax-fraud sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic withholding tax on dividend distributions by a Luxembourg SARL. Reduced to 0% for distributions meeting the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions (direct shareholding of at least 10% or EUR 1,200,000, held for at least 12 months) and under the domestic participation-exemption regime. Double tax treaty rates commonly range from 5% to 15% for portfolio investors and 0% for substantial corporate shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief at source, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent an official certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, together with a beneficial-ownership statement and, where requested, supporting substance evidence. The application must be made on the form prescribed by the ACD before the dividend payment date. If the dividend withholding tax has been deducted, a refund claim may be submitted to the ACD within the legal limitation period, generally five years. Treaty relief is denied if the shareholder is considered an artificial conduit lacking economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments made by a SARL to non-residents, including IP royalties and debt interest. As a result, DTA rates are not restrictive domestically because the statutory rate is 0%. Interest and royalty income received by the Luxembourg SARL remains subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax at the normal rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where annual controlled transactions with related parties exceed EUR 500,000. Master File is required where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeds EUR 750 million. Documentation must be contemporaneous, in line with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, and produced to the ACD within 30 days of an audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime analogous to the UAE, but the ACD applies the OECD substance principle, the GAAR under Article 6 of the Tax Adaptation Act, and EU ATAD anti-abuse rules. A SARL holding or distributing pet supplies should maintain real local substance: business premises, qualified directors/managers, effective decision-making at board meetings in Luxembourg, employee presence, local bank accounts, and substantiated commercial risk. A 'mailbox' SARL without substance will be denied treaty benefits, participation-exemption relief, and may be deemed managed outside Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — False Declaration of E-Commerce Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Stripe/PayPal settlement revenues from the SARL's books, understating online pet-product sales, fabricating supplier invoices, or concealing secondary payment accounts held by foreign affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of underpaid corporate income tax with default interest at 0.6% per month; administrative surcharge of up to 50% of the additional tax for intent; criminal prosecution for tax fraud carrying a fine of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or de facto manager who signs the false return is personally exposed to criminal conviction, joint civil liability for the SARL's unpaid taxes, attachment of personal bank accounts and assets, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox entity: no commercial activity in Luxembourg, no local employees, no physical office, no board decisions in Luxembourg, and all sales, logistics and management functions run by a foreign parent, while dividend distributions are channeled through Luxembourg to claim treaty or EU-directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and Parent-Subsidiary Directive protection; application of GAAR/ATAD; re-taxation of the global profit at the real place of management; 15% withholding tax claw-back on distributions; additional tax and late interest; criminal fines where abusive declarations are intentionally made.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a fictitious Luxembourg seat may be jointly liable for unpaid Luxembourg taxes, face criminal liability for fraudulent certification, and be subject to personal asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying exaggerated fees to foreign related parties: inflated management fees, non-arm's length inventory prices, unjustified royalties for a brand not controlled by the SARL, or failing to prepare the Local File for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD profit adjustment to the arm's length result, additional CIT and municipal business tax, irregularity interest at 0.6% per month, administrative penalties up to 30% of the reassessed tax for serious negligence, and criminal penalties if false transfer-pricing documentation is submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving sham intercompany agreements without economic substance are personally liable for the resulting tax loss; they face personal fines, disqualification, seizure of personal assets and criminal proceedings where fraudulent bookkeeping is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL's Stripe/PayPal merchant accounts to process payments for unidentifiable third-party suppliers, layering proceeds through rapid withdrawals, ignoring repeated payment-processor suspicious-activity notices, or intentionally transacting with sanctioned parties in connection with online sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where the SARL acts as an obligated entity under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004, regulatory fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; money-laundering offences may result in imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 250,000, confiscation of laundered assets, and freezing orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficiary owners and directors who participate in or knowingly disregard laundering indicators are personally liable: civil restitution, criminal fines, imprisonment, asset freeze, travel bans, and loss of director eligibility.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 510 for consecutive fiscal years while online sales continue, filing 'nil' returns while payment-processor payouts reveal undisclosed turnover, or destroying accounting records in anticipation of a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxation d'office by the ACD based on external payment processor data; late-filing fine up to EUR 5,000; default interest at 0.6% per month; loss of loss carry-forward applicability and of treaty benefits; criminal sanctions for obstruction of tax controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors causing the default assessment remain jointly and severally liable for the income tax debts when the SARL is liquidated; they may be prohibited from leaving Luxembourg pending debt settlement and risk personal bankruptcy declarations if assets were misappropriated.
